body_text: Release Details TELA Bio Announces Inducement Grants Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) August 5, 2026 PDF Version MALVERN, Pa., Aug. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TELA Bio, Inc. ("TELA Bio") (NASDAQ: TELA), a commercial-stage medical technology company focused on providing innovative soft-tissue reconstruction solutions, today announced that the Board of Directors of TELA Bio approved inducement grants of stock options to purchase an aggregate of 2,370,000 shares of its common stock and restricted stock units covering 500,000 shares of its common stock to the Company’s newly-hired Chief Executive Officer, Heather Getz, with a grant date of August 3, 2026 (the "Getz Grant Date"). The stock options consist of (i) stock options to purchase 1,365,000 shares of common stock (the “Standard Options”) and (ii) premium-priced stock options to purchase 1,005,000 shares of common stock (the “Premium-Options”). Additionally, the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors of TELA Bio approved inducement grants of restricted stock units covering 95,500 shares of its common stock to 11 newly-hired employees, with a grant date of August 4, 2026. The stock options and the restricted stock units discussed above were granted pursuant to the Nasdaq Rule 5635(c)(4) inducement grant exception as a component of Ms. Getz’s and each individual's employment compensation and were granted as an inducement material to his or her acceptance of employment with TELA Bio. The Standard Options have an exercise price equal to $0.74 per share, the closing price of TELA Bio's common stock as reported on the Nasdaq Global Market on the Getz Grant Date. The Premium-Options have an exercise price equal to $0.90 per share. The stock options each have a ten-year term and vest over four years, with 25% of the shares underlying the stock option vesting on the first anniversary of the Getz Grant Date, and the remaining 75% of the shares vesting in equal monthly installments over 36 months thereafter, subject to Ms. Getz’s continued service with TELA Bio through the applicable vesting dates. The restricted stock units will vest in equal annual installments over four years, subject to Ms. Getz’s and each individual's continued service with TELA Bio through the applicable vesting dates. About TELA Bio, Inc. TELA Bio, Inc. (NASDAQ: TELA) is a commercial-stage medical technology company focused on providing innovative technologies that optimize clinical outcomes by prioritizing the preservation and restoration of the patient's own anatomy. The Company is committed to providing surgeons with advanced, economically effective soft-tissue reconstruction solutions that leverage the patient's natural healing response while minimizing long-term exposure to permanent synthetic materials. For more information, visit www.telabio.com . body_text: Aug 05, 2026 Ingevity Releases 2025 Sustainability Report, Highlights Performance and Impact PRESS RELEASE NORTH CHARLESTON, S.C., August 5, 2026 – Ingevity Corporation (NYSE:NGVT) today announced it has published its 2025 Sustainability Report featuring the company’s advanced materials and technologies that help customers achieve environmental goals while supporting critical industries worldwide. The report, titled “A Decade of Performance, a Future of Possibility,” highlights how Ingevity’s products and operations create measurable value for customers and stakeholders. The report showcases technologies that reduce emissions, extend infrastructure life, support cleaner water and incorporate renewable raw materials. “As we mark a decade as a public company, our sustainability approach is grounded in performance, making a positive impact in the communities we serve, prioritizing safety and delivering solutions that matter to our customers,” said Dave Li, Ingevity president and CEO. “This report demonstrates how our products, people and operations continue to advance our purpose to purify, protect and enhance the world around us while creating long-term value for our stakeholders.” Ingevity’s 2025 Sustainability Report, Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) and Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) indices outline efforts to support a global vision for a more sustainable world. Except as expressly indicated otherwise, the information in the Sustainability Report and indices given is as of the date of publication, July 31, 2026. Ingevity: Purify, Protect and Enhance Ingevity (NYSE: NGVT) is a global specialty materials company that develops advanced carbon and engineered materials solutions that improve mobility, strengthen and extend the life of infrastructure and enhance industrial processes. With a 90‑year legacy of innovation, we work closely with customers to solve technical challenges and deliver materials that improve performance and environmental outcomes in essential applications. Our portfolio includes Performance Materials activated carbon technologies for emissions control and filtration; Pavement Technologies solutions for high-performance pavement applications and dispersants for crop protection; and Advanced Polymer Technologies specialty polymers for coatings and industrial applications. Headquartered in North Charleston, South Carolina, Ingevity operates from 17 locations worldwide and employs approximately 1,400 people. Learn more at ingevity.com . title: Content Audit Tips to Improve Your Rankings (August 2026)
summary: This August 2026 content audit guide shows you how to score pages, fix metadata, build an action plan, and optimize for AI citations and E-E-A-T signals.
body_text: Running a content audit sounds thorough until you're 200 URLs deep with a spreadsheet full of pages and no clear decision on what to do with any of them. The crawl isn't what moves rankings. The framework you use to decide what gets updated, what gets merged, and what gets cut is the part that matters. TLDR: Google's March 2026 Core Update hit 55% of monitored sites. A content audit turns that risk into a ranked to-do list. Every page gets one of four labels, keep, update, consolidate, or remove, then you sequence fixes by effort-to-impact ratio. Content updated within 90 days gets cited far more often in AI answers. Staleness is one of the fastest wins to fix. 96% of AI Overview citations come from sources with strong E-E-A-T signals. An author bio alone won't get you there. Maintouch flags pages with declining impressions after 90 days and runs keyword gap analysis and cannibalization detection in a single workflow. What Is a Content Audit A content audit is a systematic review of every page on your site, measured against performance data, search intent, and strategic relevance. Knowing how to run a content audit is the difference between knowing what you have and knowing what's working. Two terms worth separating: a content inventory is a catalogued list of URLs, publish dates, word counts, and metadata. A content audit layers on the evaluation, showing which pages drive traffic, which ones cannibalize each other, which have decayed past usefulness, and which deserve more investment. You need both. The inventory is the raw material. The audit turns it into a plan. Why Content Audits Improve Rankings Google's March 2026 Core Update hit 55% of monitored sites by penalizing thin content and weak E-E-A-T signals. If you haven't audited recently, there's a decent chance your site took a hit you haven't diagnosed yet. That's the point of the audit: it converts vague ranking drops into specific, fixable problems. Maybe three posts are cannibalizing the same keyword. Maybe a page that ranked well two years ago now targets an intent Google has reclassified. Without it, you're guessing at causes and applying fixes that might make things worse. Bloggers who update older posts are 2.5x more likely to report strong results . But you can't update strategically if you don't know which posts deserve the investment and which ones are dragging your domain down. Step 1: Define Your Content Audit Goals and Scope Before you pull a single URL into a spreadsheet, decide what you're actually solving for. "Audit everything" sounds thorough, but on a site with 500+ pages, it's a recipe for a stalled project that never reaches the action stage. Pick a goal first. Recovering traffic after a core update means you're focused on impression trends, ranking drops, and thin content. Improving conversions means you're looking at bounce rate, time on page, and CTA placement across bottom-of-funnel pages. A freshness push means filtering for publish dates and staleness signals. Each goal changes which metrics matter and which pages you even bother reviewing. Then scope by content type or funnel stage. I'd audit blog content separately from product pages, since the signals you're reading, and the fixes you'd apply, are completely different. Understanding where keywords sit in the buyer journey helps clarify which segment deserves priority first. A blog post losing impressions might need a full rewrite. A product page losing conversions might need better schema or a restructured CTA. Sites under 200 pages can audit everything in one pass. Above that, batch by section and work through the highest-priority segment first. Step 2: Build a Complete Content Inventory Start with a full crawl. Screaming Frog is the standard. It pulls every URL on your site, including orphan pages your sitemap misses. Export that list, then layer in Google Search Console data for clicks, impressions, and average position per URL. Neither source alone gives you the full picture. Structure your spreadsheet with these columns: URL Page title Content type (blog post, landing page, product page) Last updated date Clicks (last 90 days) Impressions (last 90 days) Average position The last-updated date column matters more than most people think. Google weighs freshness as a ranking signal, and AI engines are even more aggressive about it. Based on Maintouch internal data, content updated within the last 90 days gets cited far more often in AI answers. If you can't sort for staleness, you can't fix it. And staleness is one of the fastest wins in any audit. Don't skip orphan pages. The Screaming Frog crawl will surface URLs that aren't linked from anywhere on your site, invisible to both users and search engines. They're either wasting crawl budget or missing an internal linking opportunity that costs you nothing to close. Step 3: Score Content Performance with the Right Metrics Two categories of signals matter: quantitative and qualitative. You need both. Numbers without context lead to bad decisions. Quantitative Signals Pull these from Google Search Console and GA4: Organic clicks and impressions (trending up, flat, or declining over 90 days) Average position per page Bounce rate and time on page Conversions or goal completions The combinations tell you more than any single metric. High impressions with low CTR points to a metadata problem, where Google's showing the page, but your title or description doesn't match what the searcher actually wants. High traffic with a high bounce rate is a different animal. That's usually an intent mismatch: the page ranks for something it doesn't actually answer well. Qualitative Signals Numbers won't tell you whether your content is actually good. For that, read each page against a checklist: Does the content match current search intent? Pull up the live SERP. If Google's serving videos and listicles for your target keyword and you wrote a 3,000-word essay, you've got a format mismatch. Is the information accurate and up to date? Are internal links present and pointing somewhere useful? Does the page show real E-E-A-T signals, such as an author byline with credentials, first-party data, something that proves a human with expertise touched it? A page with strong traffic but shallow depth is a ticking clock, because it'll hold position until a competitor publishes something more thorough. A page with real depth but zero impressions usually just needs better internal linking or a metadata rewrite to get Google's attention. Step 4: The Keep, Update, Consolidate, or Remove Decision Every page in your inventory gets one of four labels: Label When to apply it Action Keep Ranking well, driving clicks, intent-aligned Light maintenance only Update Solid topic and backlinks, but impressions sliding because a competitor published something fresher or more thorough Rewrite or expand the existing page Consolidate Two or more pages targeting the same keyword, splitting authority between them Merge into one stronger piece and 301 redirect the others Remove Zero traffic, no backlinks, thin content adding crawl waste Noindex or redirect to a relevant page One word of caution on removals. Nielsen Norman Group flags this in particular: even low-traffic pages can hold residual ranking equity. Before you delete or redirect anything, check whether it has inbound links or quietly ranks for long-tail queries you haven't noticed. A careless 404 can cost you more than the page was worth keeping. Step 5: Build and Execute Your Action Plan Once every page has a label, sequence the work by effort-to-impact ratio. Start with technical and metadata fixes: broken canonicals, missing title tags, outdated schema. These take minutes per page and can move rankings within a single crawl cycle. If you've got 40 pages with missing meta descriptions, batch those in an afternoon. Next, hit high-impression, low-click pages. A title tag rewrite or a sharper meta description can lift CTR without touching the content itself, giving your fastest traffic wins, because the rankings already exist. Then move to consolidations and full rewrites. These take more time, but they carry the biggest upside for pages stuck cannibalizing each other or drifting off-intent. For each action, log the owner, deadline, and a "before" snapshot of the metric you're trying to move. Track AI visibility KPIs alongside traditional metrics so you don't miss what shifted. Without that baseline, you won't know whether the fix worked or whether something else changed at the same time. Revisit the numbers at 30 and 60 days. If a rewrite hasn't moved impressions by day 60, the problem is usually deeper than content quality. E-E-A-T in Practice When Your Content Is AI-Generated Google doesn't care whether a human or an LLM wrote the first draft. It cares whether the published page carries real authority signals. That distinction changes what you're actually checking for during the audit. Most advice stops at "add an author bio." That's table stakes. When you're auditing pages drafted with AI assistance, go deeper: Does the post have a named author with verifiable credentials, like a real LinkedIn, a body of published work, topical expertise that's checkable? Does the content show first-hand experience? Specific outcomes, original data, concrete examples from actual projects. Do external citations point to primary sources, or are they linking to secondary summaries and content aggregators? Does the schema markup accurately reflect the author and publication details? Mismatches between your Article schema and the visible byline will hurt you. Structured data for AI search has become a signal you can't treat as optional. 96% of AI Overview citations come from sources with strong E-E-A-T signals. And 41% of AI-only sites lost traffic after Google's March 2026 Core Update, while content with genuine authority signals gained rankings. The question isn't whether you used AI to write the content. The question is whether anyone with real expertise touched it before it went live. How to Audit for AI Citation Visibility A standard content audit checks whether pages rank in Google. It doesn't check whether they get cited in AI Overviews . Increasingly, those are two different things. Add an "AI citation readiness" column to your inventory spreadsheet. For each page, check: Do key answers appear in self-contained passages of 130 to 170 words within the first 30% of the content? AI engines pull from concise, complete answer blocks, never buried paragraphs. Are headings formatted as questions, with direct answers immediately following? Is FAQPage or HowTo schema implemented, and does it match what's actually on the page? Is the dateModified field current? Stale timestamps get filtered out before content quality is even considered. A page can pass your SEO audit and still be invisible to the citation layer. Treat that as its own action item, separate from any ranking fix. How Often to Run a Content Audit For most sites, every six months is the right cadence. That's frequent enough to catch algorithm changes and content decay before they compound, but not so frequent that you're re-auditing pages that haven't had time to respond to your last round of fixes. If you're publishing 15+ pieces a month or operating in a fast-moving vertical, run quarterly audits on your highest-priority pages. You don't need to re-crawl everything: focus on bottom-of-funnel and conversion content, where behavior changes hit revenue fastest. Smaller sites publishing a few times a month can stretch to annual audits without much risk. Top-of-funnel content decays slower and carries less direct revenue weight. One rule I follow regardless of site size: any time Google rolls a core update, run a targeted audit within 30 days. Don't wait for your scheduled cadence to tell you what broke. Content Audit Tools Four tool categories feed a content audit. Skip any one and you've got blind spots. Crawl tools handle inventory. Screaming Frog, Sitebulb, or a free Google Sheets script pulling your sitemap XML will get you a full URL list. The crawl catches orphan pages, broken redirects, and metadata gaps that analytics won't surface on their own. Analytics integrations give you the behavior layer. Google Search Console shows impressions, clicks, and average position. GA4 adds bounce rate, time on page, and conversion data. You need both connected to your spreadsheet, because a page can look healthy in one source and dying in the other. keyword competitor analysis like Semrush or Ahrefs fill in what Search Console misses: competitor keyword overlap, cannibalization detection, and historical ranking trends over a longer window than 90 days. Schema validators close the loop on structured data. Google's Rich Results Test and Schema Markup Validator check whether your JSON-LD actually parses and matches what's on the page. If you're auditing for AI citation readiness, this step isn't optional. None of these tools run the audit for you. They're inputs. The audit is the judgment layer you apply on top, reading the data, labeling each page, deciding what to fix first. How Maintouch Automates the Content Audit Workflow Most of what I've walked through above, Maintouch runs automatically in the background for every paying account. The automatic content refresh system watches for the exact trigger conditions you'd otherwise check manually: any page indexed for over 90 days with declining impressions gets flagged. Once flagged, the system surfaces recommended changes, regenerates metadata, refreshes internal links using live Search Console ranking data, and updates schema on every publish. You're not building a spreadsheet and sorting by staleness. It's already done. The General Agent handles keyword gap analysis, cannibalization detection, and zero-volume query discovery inside a single conversational workflow, replacing the Semrush-plus-Ahrefs-plus-spreadsheet stack most teams duct-tape together for a manual audit. If you're running a B2B SEO strategy and publishing regularly, the audit cycle stops being a quarterly fire drill and starts running continuously in the background. Shoot me a message at [email protected] if you want to see what that looks like on your site. Final Thoughts on Improving Rankings Through Content Audits The sites that recover fastest after core updates aren't the ones with the biggest budgets. They're the ones who know exactly which pages need attention and in what order. That's what a good content audit gives you, and it doesn't require a quarterly fire drill to get there. Shoot me a message at [email protected] if you want to see what it looks like running on your site. FAQ What does E-E-A-T actually look like in practice when most of your content is AI-generated? Adding an author bio is the starting point, not the finish line. For AI-assisted content, E-E-A-T means a named author with a verifiable LinkedIn and a body of published work, first-hand experience signals like specific outcomes and original data, external citations pointing to primary sources instead of content aggregators, and Article schema that accurately reflects the byline visible on the page. The question Google is asking is whether someone with real expertise touched the content before it went live, and 96% of AI Overview citations come from sources that can show that clearly. How do you optimize content to get cited by Perplexity, ChatGPT, and other AI engines? AI engines pull from self-contained answer blocks of 130 to 170 words that appear within the first 30% of the page and name the entity inside the block. Structure headings as direct questions with the answer in the first sentence immediately following, implement FAQPage or HowTo schema that matches what's actually on the page, and keep the dateModified field current since stale timestamps get filtered out before content quality is even considered. A page can rank well in Google and still be invisible to the citation layer if those structural signals are missing. How often should you run a content audit? For most sites, every six months is the right cadence for a full audit. Sites publishing 15 or more pieces per month should run quarterly audits on their highest-priority pages, focused on bottom-of-funnel and conversion content where behavior changes hit revenue fastest. One rule that holds regardless of site size: any time Google rolls a core update, run a targeted audit within 30 days instead of waiting for your scheduled cadence. What's the difference between a content audit and a content inventory? A content inventory is a catalogued list of URLs, publish dates, word counts, and metadata. A content audit layers on the evaluation: which pages drive traffic, which ones cannibalize each other, which have decayed past usefulness, and which deserve more investment. You need both, because the inventory is the raw material and the audit is the analysis that turns it into a sequenced action plan. What's the best alternative to Semrush or Ahrefs for a B2B SaaS startup that wants execution over data reporting? Semrush and Ahrefs are data tools: they surface what needs doing and stop there, leaving remediation to your team. For a B2B SaaS startup that wants the full loop closed, Maintouch runs keyword gap analysis, content creation, technical SEO fixes, backlink procurement, and citation tracking inside one system without handing work back to a developer or agency. Every paying account includes a dedicated account strategist on weekly standing syncs, which replaces the contractor layer that tools like Profound typically require on top of the subscription. How do I know which pages to rank first when I have hundreds of URLs to audit? Start by filtering for two groups: pages with high impressions and declining clicks (quick metadata wins), and pages generating zero impressions for more than six months (removal or consolidation candidates). Bottom-of-funnel pages, conversion pages, and any content tied to your top five target keywords should always be reviewed first, since changes there hit revenue fastest. The goal is sequencing by effort-to-impact ratio, not auditing alphabetically. What's the risk of redirecting or deleting a low-traffic page? Before you remove anything, check whether the page holds inbound links or ranks for long-tail queries that don't show up in your main keyword reports. A page with 10 monthly clicks might be the only URL earning you a backlink from a high-authority domain. If it does have link equity, redirect it to the most topically relevant page instead of returning a 404, which drops that equity entirely. What's keyword cannibalization and how do I find it during a content audit? Keyword cannibalization is when two or more pages on your site target the same query, splitting authority and confusing Google about which one to rank. To surface it, export your Search Console data, group URLs by their primary keyword, and flag any keyword matched to more than one URL with meaningful impressions. The fix is consolidation: merge the weaker page into the stronger one and 301 redirect the old URL. How long does it take to see results after updating content from a content audit? Metadata fixes like title tag rewrites can move CTR within a single crawl cycle, sometimes within days. Rewrites and consolidations typically take 30 to 60 days to show ranking movement, depending on how quickly Google recrawls the page and how competitive the keyword is. If a rewrite hasn't moved impressions within 60 days, the problem is usually deeper than the content itself, for example a structural intent mismatch or a backlink gap. Do I need to run a technical SEO audit separately from a content audit? They overlap more than most people treat them. A content audit that ignores broken canonicals, slow load times, and crawl errors will miss some of the reasons pages aren't ranking despite solid content. I'd run the crawl tool and the content spreadsheet at the same time, then fix technical issues first since they affect every page and often take less time to resolve than a full content rewrite. How does content quality affect AI Overview citations compared to regular Google rankings? For Google rankings, content quality competes on depth, relevance, and authority relative to other pages in the results. For AI Overview citations, the bar is structural: self-contained answer blocks of 130 to 170 words, headings formatted as direct questions, current dateModified timestamps, and accurate schema markup. A page can rank on page one of Google and still be excluded from AI citations if those structural signals are missing, which is why auditing for AI citation readiness is a separate check from standard SEO scoring. Can Maintouch run a content audit automatically instead of using a spreadsheet? Yes. Maintouch watches for pages indexed for over 90 days with declining impressions and flags them automatically, so you're not manually sorting a spreadsheet for staleness. The General Agent handles keyword gap analysis and cannibalization detection inside a single conversational workflow, and the content refresh system regenerates metadata, updates internal links using live Search Console data, and refreshes schema on every publish. If you're publishing regularly, the audit cycle runs continuously in the background instead of as a quarterly project.

title: Madrigal Pharmaceuticals to Participate in the Canaccord Genuity 45th Annual Growth Conference

body_text: Madrigal Pharmaceuticals to Participate in the Canaccord Genuity 45th Annual Growth Conference August 6, 2026 PDF Version CONSHOHOCKEN, Pa., Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Madrigal Pharmaceuticals, Inc. title: How to Accept Payments from Indian Customers Without a Local Entity
summary: Learn how foreign businesses can accept payments from India using UPI, RuPay, and INR settlements without GST registration or local incorporation.
body_text: Table of Contents Toggle Yes, foreign businesses can accept INR and UPI payments from Indian customers without opening a local company by using an RBI-authorized PA-CB (Payment Aggregator Cross-Border) payment provider like Cashfree. This allows international merchants to collect payments via UPI, RuPay, cards, and Net Banking while settling funds in USD, EUR, GBP, and other currencies. Spend ten minutes in any founder forum about selling to India and you will hit the same line. “But you don’t have an Indian entity.” It lands like a full stop, as though a missing Indian company is the one thing standing between you and the market. It used to be closer to true than it is now. The phrase still means something, and it is worth knowing exactly what an Indian entity does and does not buy you before you spend a quarter and a lawyer’s retainer setting one up. Why is India’s Payment Ecosystem Unlike Any Other Market? India’s digital payment system is built to handle the volume of transactions, which makes it fundamentally different from most global markets. Within this system, the most common failure point is not pricing or logistics, but payment compatibility. For a foreign merchant, enabling Visa and MasterCard is enough to accept payments from Indian customers. But that’s not the case. 1. United Payment Interface (UPI) UPI is not just another payment option in India. For many Indian consumers, it has become the default way to pay online, and it began in 2016 with the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). For Indians, UPI is not an alternative but the default payment method. It plays a role similar to cards in the US or iDEAL in the Netherlands. This payment method allows real-time bank-to-bank transfers through applications like; GooglePay, PhonePe and Paytm No card details, no OTP – users just need to enter the amount, authenticate the payment with UPI PIN and in some supported flows, biometric authentication is also available. So, one of the reasons why foreign businesses ask why my India payments are failing on my international website is that they have not enabled UPI. Therefore, if you want to accept UPI payments as a foreign company, your payment stack must connect to India’s domestic payments ecosystem rather than relying only on international card rails. 2. RuPay Card Network – Often Ignored by Global Merchants Where Visa and MasterCard are foreign-born, RuPay is an Indian-made card payment network system. Launched in 2012 by the NPCI , RuPay is the local alternative to Visa and MasterCard. Today, RuPay has seen large-scale issuance in India, with public references citing over 750 million RuPay cards issued. Not adding RuPay to your payments infrastructure means missing out on a huge potential customer base. If your checkout only supports Visa or Mastercard, you are excluding a meaningful portion of Indian consumers before the transaction even begins. 3. RBI-Mandated OTP Transactions The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) oversees all financial systems in India, and as per the central bank’s requirements, OTP is required for authentication. Indian digital payments are subject to RBI authentication requirements. For online card payments, this means Additional Factor of Authentication (AFA)/2FA, often implemented through OTP-based flows, though newer frameworks allow other approved authentication factors. Some international websites see materially higher failure rates on Indian transactions when their checkout is not optimised for local payment methods and authentication flows. These are some of the core payment behaviours foreign merchants need to account for. Along with this, there’s also Net Banking and EMI options, which customers also expect to see on the payments page. What are the Key Entities Involved in India’s Payment Ecosystem? Entity Role in India’s Payments Ecosystem RBI (Reserve Bank of India) India’s central bank and payments regulator NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India) Operator of UPI and RuPay UPI (Unified Payments Interface) Real-time bank-to-bank payment network RuPay India’s domestic card network PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm Major UPI payment applications AFA / OTP RBI-mandated additional authentication for card payments Visa / Mastercard International card networks with limited India-specific optimization What are the Two Ways to Accept INR Payments as a Foreign Business? 1. Incorporation Route Until recently, many foreign businesses looking to collect INR payments from Indian customers often considered local incorporation as the default route. Incorporate an Indian Private Limited company under the Companies Act, 2013 Appoint local directors Open an Indian bank account Register for GST Hire a Chartered Accountant (CA) for ongoing compliance Apply to a domestic payment aggregator for merchant onboarding Following this process, it can take 3 to 6 months before you can start collecting payments. But this method also creates operational overheads like GST filings , compliance reporting, accounting, and more. For international brands that are only testing the Indian market, this method drains resources, time, and effort without any ROI guarantee. 2. Payment Aggregator-Cross Border (PA-CB) Route – Recommended Since 2023, the Reserve Bank of India has formally enabled the PA-CB (Payment Aggregator Cross-Border) framework under FEMA (Foreign Exchange Management Act). This framework allows RBI-licensed PA-CB providers to onboard foreign merchants directly, without requiring local incorporation. Under this model, businesses selling to Indian customers can; Accept INR payments through UPI, RuPay, Visa, Mastercard, and Net banking. Receive and settle payments in USD, EUR, GBP and other foreign currencies. Get FEMA compliance. Consolidated under the RBI (Regulation of Payment Aggregators) Directions, 2025, this framework governs all cross-border digital payments between Indian customers and international merchants. Here’s how it works: An Indian customer pays a foreign merchant in INR. The payment is processed by an RBI-licensed PA-CB provider. The INR funds move into an InCA (Inward Collection Account). The InCA is maintained with an Authorized Dealer Category-I (AD-I) bank. The AD bank performs foreign exchange conversion. The converted amount is remitted to the foreign merchant’s overseas bank account in USD, EUR, GBP, or another supported currency. Under RBI’s 2025 PA Directions, PA-CB transactions are capped at ₹25 lakh per transaction. Cashfree is a PA-CB provider , which means when you partner with us, you don’t need to be an Indian company, have an Indian bank account, or have GST registration. The PA-CB provider handles the regulation part and provides the payment infrastructure layer, which includes; Merchant KYC (Know Your Customer) and CDD (Customer Due Diligence) FEMA compliance workflows Purpose-code tagging for remittances FX conversion through AD banks e-FIRC (Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate) generation for transaction records Local Entity vs PA-CB Comparison Feature Local Entity Route PA-CB Route Indian Company Required Yes No Indian Bank Account Required Not required GST Registration Usually required Depends on business model Time to Go Live 3–6 months As fast as 48 hours UPI Support Yes Yes Compliance Burden High Lower FX Settlement Manual setup Managed by provider Role of Each Entity in Building Your Payment Infrastructure Entity Role RBI (Reserve Bank of India) India’s payments regulator PA-CB Framework governing cross-border payment aggregation FEMA India’s foreign exchange regulatory law InCA (Inward Collection Account) Account where INR funds are collected before FX conversion AD Bank (Authorized Dealer Bank) RBI-authorized bank handling foreign exchange conversion e-FIRC Proof of inward foreign remittance KYC / CDD Merchant identity verification and compliance checks Cashfree Payments RBI-licensed PA-CB provider How Money Flows from the Customer’s Account to your Bank Account? Foreign merchants often hesitate to enter India because they cannot clearly see how funds move across borders compliantly. The PA-CB model solves this by creating a regulated settlement chain from the Indian customer to your overseas account. Here’s how the process works; Payment Initiation: An Indian customer makes the payment using UPI, RuPay, Visa, Mastercard, or Net Banking, and this transaction is processed in INR. Cashfree Captures the Transaction: Cashfree, working as an RBI-licensed PA-CB provider, processes the payment and routes the funds into an Inward Collection Account (InCA). This account is maintained with an Authorized Dealer Category-I (AD-I) bank in India. FX Conversion: Once funds are added to the InCA, the bank will convert INR into your preferred settlement currency, and here, Cashfree does not take any FX Markup fees from overseas businesses on the conversion process. Overseas Settlement Completes: The converted funds are remitted to your overseas bank account through SWIFT/wire transfer infrastructure. Most eligible merchants receive settlement on a T+1 business day basis. Documentation: Every settlement includes an e-FIRC (electronic Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate), which is the official proof of inward foreign remittance and is needed for compliance and accounting purposes under FEMA. How to Sell to Indian Customers from Abroad with Cashfree? Cashfree has made an easy and business-friendly onboarding process for foreign merchants. Within 48 hours of onboarding, you can start accepting payments from Indian customers . 1. Prepare Documentation Collect all documents, including; Business registration certificate from your home country Proof of business address Director or authorized signatory ID (passport or national ID) Overseas bank account details for settlements Website or app URL with a clear product or service description 2. Complete Merchant Onboarding Sign up through Cashfree’s international merchant onboarding flow as we directly onboard foreign entities under the RBI PA-CB framework. For this process, you don’t need to be an Indian co-founder, local director, or even an Indian entity. Cashfree conducts merchant KYC (Know Your Customer) and CDD (Customer Due Diligence) as required under RBI regulations. 3. Choose your Integration Method Integration method depends on your technical setup, including; No-Code: Payment links and payment pages are added for instant INR collection. E-Commerce Plugins: Integrate your Shopify and Magento store with Cashfree. REST APIs: Completely customized checkout integration supporting all payment methods, including UPI app launch, payment links and UPI mandates. 4. Testing and Go-Live We allow businesses to test transactions inside a Sandbox environment before full-scale production deployment. We deliver a robust payments system allowing businesses and merchants to go live within 48 hours using a 99.99% uptime SLA backed infrastructure. 5. Operations Management With Cashfree, you get an operations dashboard where you can track payments, see settlement visibility, manage refunds, reconcile exports, and download e-FIRC documentation. What Does it Cost to Accept Payments from Indian Customers Without a Local Entity? Transparency in pricing matters because cross-border payments have several hidden costs inside FX spreads and settlement delays. Payment system providers charge businesses based on business category, payment method mix, and processing volume. Out of all, FX conversion is the most important cost. Payment providers like Cashfree offer transparent FX on settlement, and the conversion is handled at the prevailing interbank market rate through RBI-authorized AD-I banking partners. This is significant for an international business because many cross-border payment providers quietly add 1–4% FX markup inside the conversion rate itself. Hidden Cost Checklist: Questions to Ask Any Provider: Is there an FX markup beyond the published transaction fee? Are settlement delays contractually built into payouts? Is e-FIRC documentation included or billed separately? Are refunds charged as additional transactions? Are there minimum processing commitments or monthly platform fees? Conclusion The modern era of India’s payment ecosystem does not require foreign businesses to choose between compliance and speed. With zero local incorporation, without opening a bank account, or without building a separate entity, overseas businesses can start accepting payments from Indian customers. The RBI’s PA-CB framework and the payment providers authorized to use this framework allow cross-border transactions while staying compliant. Now, your customers can pay without any issues because they can pay through UPI, the most common digital payment method used in India today. Ready to Accept Payments from Indian Customers? Get started with Cashfree’s international merchant onboarding and accept UPI payments from customers in India. Get Started with Cashfree FAQs Can a foreign company accept UPI payments without a local entity in India? Yes, foreign companies can accept UPI payments by either registering as a local entity or by partnering with an RBI-authorized PA-CB compliant provider like Cashfree. The PA-CB route allows international businesses to accept payments in their local currency without registering their firm in India. What is the RBI PA-CB framework? The PA-CB (Payment Aggregator Cross-Border) framework allows licensed payment providers to process cross-border transactions between Indian customers and overseas businesses compliantly. Do I need to register for GST in India to sell to Indian customers? PA-CB does not require you to incorporate locally just to collect payments. However, GST or other tax obligations may still apply depending on what you sell, your operating model, and applicable Indian tax rules. Businesses should consult a tax advisor. Do I need an Indian bank account to collect payments from India? No. With a PA-CB provider, payments are collected in INR and settled directly into your overseas bank account in your preferred currency. Which Indian payment methods should international businesses support? International businesses should support; UPI, RuPay, Visa, Mastercard, Net Banking and EMI options What currencies can foreign businesses settle in? Most PA-CB providers support settlements in; USD, EUR, GBP, SGD, AED, and other major currencies. How long does it take to start accepting Indian payments as a foreign company? Taking the old route, where you must first incorporate your company in India, get a GST number, get all permissions, and get FEMA compliance, means spending at least 15 to 20 days. With Cashfree, eligible merchants can go live quickly, subject to documentation, KYC/risk checks, integration readiness, and approval. Is there a transaction limit for cross-border payments in India? Under the Regulation of Payment Aggregators) Directions, 2025, the maximum transaction value permitted for inward cross-border payments is ₹25,00,000 per transaction. Any amount above this will require alternative methods as stated under the FEMA regulations.

title: Mercado global: Quais os melhores países para vender internacionalmente?
summary: Aqui vão as principais informações que você precisa saber sobre o mercado global
body_text: Expandir seu e-commerce para o mundo pode parecer um baita desafio, mas a real é que nunca foi tão fácil ganhar dinheiro vendendo para fora! Com a digitalização do comércio e a logística internacional cada vez mais acessível, dar esse passo pode ser o que falta para seu negócio decolar. Mas será que vale a pena? E para onde mirar suas vendas? Bora descobrir! Por que entrar no mercado global de e-commerce? Se você tem uma loja online, já deve ter sacado que o mercado nacional tem seus limites. Expandir para o exterior é um jeito incrível de alcançar mais clientes, diversificar os ganhos e, claro, lucrar mais! Sem contar que alguns produtos fazem ainda mais sucesso lá fora do que aqui. Outro ponto top é a sazonalidade. Enquanto no Brasil a Black Friday bomba em novembro, na China o grande evento é o Dia dos Solteiros (11/11), e por aí vai. Se posicionar bem nessas datas pode fazer seu faturamento explodir! E sabe o que é melhor? Ferramentas como Cartpanda, deixa tudo mais simples. Dá para vender em moeda estrangeira, usar gateways de pagamento internacionais e até automatizar fretes globais. Ou seja, sem desculpas para não pensar grande! Principais desafios e benefícios desse mercado Antes de sair vendendo para todo canto, bora entender os prós e contras de ser um player global? Vantagens de vender lá fora: Mais oportunidades de venda : Seu produto pode ser um hit internacional! Ganhos em moeda forte : Dólar, euro... já pensou faturar em moeda valorizada? Menos concorrência em certos nichos : Em alguns países, você pode encontrar pouca competição. Expansão da marca : Se tornar uma marca global dá um baita peso para sua reputação. Desafios que você precisa considerar: Burocracia e impostos : Cada país tem suas regras, e é bom se preparar para isso. Logística : Enviar produtos para longe pode ser caro e exigir bons parceiros de transporte. Atendimento ao cliente : Se vender para outros países, vai precisar atender clientes em outros idiomas. Adaptação ao mercado local : Marketing, site, embalagem... pode ser que precise ajustar tudo para conquistar o público-alvo. Quais os melhores países para vender? Agora vamos ao que interessa: quais os melhores mercados para explorar? Se liga nessa lista! 1. Estados Unidos O paraíso do e-commerce! Os americanos compram muito online e já estão acostumados a comprar de lojas internacionais. A concorrência é alta, mas as oportunidades são gigantes. 2. Canadá Menos populoso que os EUA, mas com consumidores de alto poder aquisitivo. Além disso, a proximidade com os Estados Unidos facilita muito a logística. 3. Europa (Reino Unido, Alemanha e França) Público exigente, mas disposto a pagar mais por produtos de qualidade. Alemanha e Reino Unido são líderes de compras online na Europa. O maior desafio? Regulamentações e diferentes idiomas. 4. Austrália Mercado promissor, com menos concorrência que os EUA. O único problema é a distância, que pode encarecer o frete. 5. China Gigante do e-commerce! Mas entrar nesse mercado exige estratégia e adaptação para plataformas locais como Alibaba e JD.com. 6. América Latina Se quiser expandir sem ir tão longe, países latinos como México e Argentina são ótimas opções. E o melhor: a cultura e o idioma são mais próximos do que mercados europeus ou asiáticos. Conclusão Vender para o mundo pode parecer um passo gigante, mas com planejamento e as ferramentas certas, seu e-commerce pode faturar alto em mercados internacionais! Os melhores destinos vão depender do seu nicho, mas países como EUA, Canadá, Alemanha, Austrália e China são ótimos pontos de partida. E aí, bora transformar sua loja em um e-commerce global? A Cartpanda pode te ajudar a alcançar clientes no mundo inteiro. Quem sabe sua próxima venda não vem do outro lado do planeta?

title: Building Career Opportunities in Latin America as the Region’s No. 1 Best Place to Work

body_text: Listen to this article 0:00 Hilton named No. 1 Best Workplace in Latin America by Great Place to Work, marking four consecutive years as Latin America’s top hospitality workplace Hilton’s recognition as the No. 1 Best Workplace in Latin America by Great Place to Work reflects its people-first culture and commitment to creating opportunities for team members to learn, grow and build meaningful careers across the region. Internal survey data highlights strong confidence in Hilton’s workplace culture, with 85% of team members saying they can achieve their career goals at Hilton, 88% reporting opportunities to learn and grow, and 93% saying Hilton is a great place to work. Every memorable stay, warm welcome and exceptional experience at a Hilton property starts with a team member who is committed to creating a reliable and friendly stay. Their passion and dedication create a culture that makes Hilton not only a great place to stay, but also a best place to work, learn, grow and thrive. After returning home, Isac enrolled in English classes, recognizing that language skills could open additional opportunities throughout Hilton's global network. title: Team Takeoff in Electrical Estimating: Splitting the Work Without Splitting the Accuracy
summary: Read the latest AI news and insights on OpenTools.
body_text: Most electrical estimating teams aren't large. Two or three people handling everything from plan review to bid submission is the norm, not the exception — and when a deadline compresses, the question of whether the work can be split without creating inconsistencies becomes urgent. Choosing the right takeoff tool for electricians has a lot to do with how the platform handles collaboration, because splitting a takeoff across multiple estimators is only useful if the output comes back together as a coherent, consistent document rather than three different versions of the same project. The Problem With Splitting Takeoffs Manually The instinct to divide a large drawing set by floor, system, or sheet range is sound. The execution in a manual workflow is where it breaks down. When two estimators are working from separate spreadsheets on the same project, version control becomes an immediate liability. Which file is current? Were the addenda applied to both? Did the estimator working on power use the same device library as the one working on lighting? These questions don't have clean answers in a manual environment. The reconciliation step — merging two independently produced spreadsheets into a single coherent quantity report — can take as long as one of the original takeoffs did. And it introduces a category of error that neither estimator made individually: the errors that arise from combining mismatched data. Can Multiple Estimators Work on Takeoffs Simultaneously? The practical answer depends entirely on the platform. In a spreadsheet environment, simultaneous work on the same file is possible but fragile — shared drives introduce version conflicts, and real‑time collaboration tools like Google Sheets weren't designed for the complexity of a full electrical quantity report. The result is usually that estimators divide the work, complete it separately, and reconcile afterward. Purpose‑built platforms handle this differently. Drawer AI's Enterprise tier includes full team access today, and a real‑time multi‑user workspace is on its published roadmap — designed to let multiple estimators work within a single shared project environment, so device counts, routing decisions, and QA flags are visible to the whole team rather than living in separate files that have to be merged first. The goal is to move reconciliation from a manual data‑merging exercise to a collaborative review process — a fundamentally different kind of work. The reconciliation problem doesn't disappear entirely, but it moves from a manual data‑merging exercise to a collaborative review process — which is a fundamentally different kind of work. How Takeoff Software Integrates With Estimating Workflows Understanding how takeoff software integrates with estimating workflows requires looking at what happens after the quantity report is generated — not just how it's produced. A takeoff that lives in a proprietary format and can't be exported cleanly creates a different kind of bottleneck than the one it was meant to solve. The integration points that matter most for team‑based workflows: Export format compatibility – structured Excel output that imports directly into estimating and ERP platforms without reformatting Revision tracking – when addenda are processed, the change log should be visible to every team member, not just the estimator who uploaded the new sheets QA handoff – the ability to flag uncertain items for a second estimator to review, rather than sending a completed file with no indication of where confidence is lower Audit trail – a record of what was counted, from which drawing version, and by whom — useful when scope disputes arise months into the project Each of these is a workflow integration point that affects not just how the takeoff is produced, but how it's used by the broader team from bid submission through construction. Best Cloud Takeoff Software for Small Electrical Contractors: What the Evaluation Actually Looks Like When small electrical contracting teams evaluate the best cloud takeoff software, the collaboration features are often the last thing examined — behind accuracy claims, pricing, and ease of use. That's a sequencing problem. For a two‑person estimating team, the ability to divide a large project and maintain a single source of truth is often more operationally valuable than marginal improvements in device detection speed. The questions worth asking before committing to a platform: Does the software support simultaneous work on the same project? Not just shared file access — actual multi‑user collaboration within a single project environment. Is the revision history visible to the full team? When drawings change, every estimator working on the project needs to know what changed and where — not just the person who uploaded the new files. Can QA tasks be assigned to specific team members? Flagging uncertain items for a second review is only useful if the platform supports routing those flags to the right person. Does the export format work with your existing estimating tools? A takeoff that requires significant reformatting before it can be used downstream adds time that negates part of the efficiency gain. What happens when the team grows? A platform that works for two estimators should scale to five without requiring a full workflow rebuild. For small firms evaluating options, Drawer AI's Enterprise tier has a multi‑user workspace, admin controls, and SSO/permission management on its published roadmap — features aimed directly at the version control and visibility problems that typically make team‑based takeoff difficult in spreadsheet environments. (Team access itself is live today on Enterprise.) The Accuracy Argument Speed is the most visible benefit of splitting a takeoff across multiple estimators. Accuracy is the one that matters more. A divided takeoff that produces inconsistent output — different device standards, different routing assumptions, different interpretations of the same panel schedule — doesn't save time overall. It moves the problem from the counting phase to the reconciliation phase, where it's harder to catch and more expensive to fix. The platforms that solve this problem don't just allow collaboration — they enforce consistency. Shared symbol libraries, centralized project settings, and unified export formats mean that two estimators working on different sections of the same drawing set produce output that fits together without manual correction. That's the standard worth holding any cloud‑based takeoff tool to.

title: TikTok Affiliate Marketing Programs: The key guide

body_text: How should brands choose TikTok affiliate marketing programs? Choose a program by reviewing eligibility, product fit, commission terms, tracking, compliance, and operating demands. A high commission rate cannot offset weak demand, a poor product page, delayed fulfillment, or unclear attribution. Define your customer, product category, average order value, target margin, and content formats before recruiting creators. The right tiktok affiliate marketing programs should give creators a clear reason to promote the product and your team reliable visibility into clicks, orders, refunds, and payments. Review access rules before outreach. Standard TikTok Shop entry commonly includes a 1,000-follower threshold, according to TikTok Shop guidance . Eligibility also varies by account status, location, age, verification, and available creator pathways. If you are researching how to become a TikTok affiliate without 1k followers, check the current in-app application flow and official documentation. Reports from Olavivo do not guarantee approval, reach, or income. Assess the financial terms in writing. JoinBrands reports rates of approximately 5% to 20% per sale in its TikTok affiliate research . Confirm whether the rate applies to the item price, excludes shipping and taxes, changes during promotions, or is reduced after a return. Establish rules for gifted products, samples, coupon codes, paid usage rights, livestream content, and order disputes. Creators should confirm payout timing and identity verification requirements before producing content. Run a controlled affiliate pilot A pilot replaces assumptions with evidence. Recruit a small group of creators whose audience, tone, location, and content quality match the buyer. Give each partner a concise brief covering product benefits, prohibited claims, disclosure language, demonstration guidance, and the submission deadline. Track views, watch time, click-through rate, and product-page visits. Measure add-to-cart activity, conversion rate, revenue per creator, and refund rate. Compare creative angles, offers, and creator segments. Retain partners who generate qualified traffic and completed orders. These measures reveal whether content creates buying intent, not merely attention. They also inform inventory planning, product-page improvements, commission adjustments, and decisions about paid amplification. Build a scalable creator workflow Spreadsheets become difficult to maintain as campaigns grow. Centralized creator profiles, outreach records, agreements, product seeding, content approvals, affiliate links, commission data, and payment status reduce missed follow-ups and reporting errors. AI-assisted discovery can organize applicants by niche, audience signals, engagement quality, and commercial relevance. Human review still matters for brand safety, disclosure, product accuracy, and authenticity. Teams should verify Reacher capabilities before using it to organize creator activity, review campaign performance, or reduce administrative effort as recruitment expands. Judge the program by repeatable revenue rather than isolated success stories. A creator reporting substantial monthly earnings may have unusual audience trust, strong product timing, or an effective content format. Ask for verifiable performance context, test several creative angles, and document which combinations produce profitable orders. Brands should also follow the required disclosure principles for sponsored and affiliate content, making material connections clear and easy for viewers to understand. Affiliate marketing works best when creators disclose relationships and recommend products that genuinely fit their audience. Reviewing the affiliate marketing model can help new partners understand referrals, attribution, and commissions. Platform rules and commerce features change over time. Teams should monitor the latest information about TikTok when planning creator campaigns and documenting operating procedures.

body_text: View All News York Space Systems Announces Chief Financial Officer Transition August 5, 2026 Download (opens in new window) DENVER--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- York Space Systems (York) (NYSE: YSS) today announced that Kevin Messerle, will step down from his current role as Chief Financial Officer. York has named Brian Frantz, currently Chief Accounting Officer, as interim CFO, effective August 14, 2026. York wishes Messerle well in his next chapter outside the industry. Frantz brings more than three decades of financial leadership experience, having held both CFO and CAO roles across public and private companies throughout his career, including prior service as CFO of RE/MAX International and as Principal Financial Officer of Intrepid Potash, Inc. (NYSE: IPI). He joined York as Chief Accounting Officer and played a central role in leading the company's transition to a public company, with direct responsibility for financial reporting, internal controls, and SEC compliance. “Brian’s CFO and CAO experience for both public and private companies, coupled with his institutional knowledge of York, and the strong working partnership we’ve built through our pubic-company transition position him well to lead York’s finance organization and keep us focused on what matters most, executing our strategy and delivering for our customers and shareholders,” said Dirk Wallinger, CEO of York. York will report second quarter 2026 financial results on August 13, 2026 and Messerle will remain in his role as Chief Financial Officer of York through the filing of the Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the second quarter of 2026. About York Space Systems York Space Systems (NYSE: YSS) is a leading, U.S.-based national defense and commercial prime providing a comprehensive suite of mission-critical solutions for national security, government, and commercial customers. York is one of the only space and defense primes with proprietary hardware and software capabilities designed to address customers’ complex mission requirements across the critical elements of the entire space ecosystem throughout the mission lifecycle. York is purpose built to address evolving national security space challenges and to adapt to the ongoing shift in the U.S. government’s mission needs and procurement processes. title: Workhorse Group Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
summary: DETROIT, Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Workhorse Group Inc. (NASDAQ: WKHS) ("Workhorse" or the "Company"), an American Industrial…...
body_text: Workhorse Group Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results August 13, 2026 • 4:05 PM EDT Download as PDF Related Documents Earnings Webcast Audio Presentation PDF 10-Q Filing HTML PDF XBRL ZIP DETROIT, Aug. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Workhorse Group Inc . (NASDAQ: WKHS) ("Workhorse" or the "Company"), an American Industrial Technology company today reported financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 and provided an update on its recent announcement about a new product line. “As we complete the final stages of merger integration, Workhorse is transforming from a pure-play manufacturer of electric commercial vehicles into a new, American industrial technology company built to serve critical commercial, government, defense, and infrastructure markets,” said Scott Griffith, CEO of Workhorse. “At the heart of this transformation is our foundational expertise in the design, engineering, testing, validation and manufacturing of industrial products. While traditionally this expertise has been applied to the commercial vehicle market, we believe we are positioned to leverage it for broader industrial applications, opening up access to additional large, high-growth markets.” The Company has spent the first half of 2026 reducing costs to manufacture its flagship commercial electric vehicles through smart engineering, strategic supply chain use and the elimination of redundant operations and facilities. In addition, it has continued work on its lower-cost and more flexible next-generation platforms which the Company believes will enable the production of a wider variety of models that can meet the needs of a larger share of the medium-duty commercial truck segment. “We believe the combination of our new enterprise sales strategy, the 2026 promotional pricing, and the strong TCO and on-road performance of our W56 step van product line is continuing to drive product enthusiasm and market interest,” said Griffith. “We have a growing backlog of firm orders and our sales pipeline has more than doubled since the start of 2026.” In addition to the strategic efforts designed to grow market share in the commercial trucking market, the Company has announced its intent to leverage its expertise and manufacturing capabilities to enter a new market. In July, Workhorse announced its intent to manufacture a turnkey, compute-ready, mobile AI data center designed for the localized infrastructure needs of distributed AI deployments. The Company believes that this new line of business can leverage current capabilities and assets to offer a compelling value proposition to a high-growth market. Second Quarter and Recent Strategic Highlights Merger Integration on Track: The Company continued integrating enterprise technology systems and reducing redundancies across facilities and personnel during the quarter. The Company continues to expect to exit 2026 at a $20 million annualized cost synergy run rate. Bill of Materials Cost Reduction Advancing: Engineering and design work on the Company's modular chassis program is progressing on schedule. Workhorse has begun discussions with new suppliers for key components expected to reduce vehicle costs and continues to work with existing suppliers on further cost reductions. These efforts, together with the Company's planned entry into the Class 5/6 cab-chassis segment, are designed to expand Workhorse's addressable market beyond its step van business and into a broader range of Class 5-6 truck types, including box trucks, representing a larger share of the $23 billion medium-duty truck market1. The modular chassis is the first step in a broader strategy to commonize hardware and software across all product lines, with production for the new chassis platform expected to begin in late 2027. Optimizing for Rapid Production Ramp: Workhorse increased production in the second quarter and continued building efficiencies across its supply chain and manufacturing processes. The Company expects to produce more fully electrified Class 5/6 chassis over the next five months than in any prior five-month period in its history. Driven by a new strategic enterprise sales approach, the total cost of ownership and performance advantages of with W56, and the Company's promotional pricing on the W56 step van, demand is building from both existing and new customers for deliveries in late 2026 and early 2027. Leadership Team Strengthened: In July, Workhorse announced the appointment of Jody Davis as Chief Financial Officer. Davis brings approximately 15 years of finance leadership across manufacturing, energy storage, aerospace, and technology companies, with a track record of closing large capital rounds and guiding development-stage businesses into full production. He has built the financial infrastructure that capital-intensive companies require as they move from development into commercialization -- precisely where Workhorse is in its journey. Entry into Mobile AI Data Center Market: In July, Workhorse announced its planned entry into the containerized mobile AI data center category, targeting an estimated $41 billion market by 20312. The Company believes its engineering competencies in power electronics, thermal management, ruggedized enclosures, mobile connectivity, vibration isolation, and embedded systems can translate directly to containerized platforms that must meet the operating demands of AI hardware in the field. The Company's go-to-market approach for this new product line is partnership-based, with Workhorse intending to serve as the design, engineering and manufacturing partner while strategic partners lead end-market development and manage customer relationships, an approach intended to reduce execution risk. The Company is targeting 2027 for commencement of initial production and commercial deliveries. ____________________ 1 Represents annual forecast of vehicle registrations as of Q1 2026 Forecast per S&P Global Mobility for NTEA US Commercial Vehicle Market Report, multiplied by an assumed $100,000 value per ICE truck and $250,000 for electric truck. 2 Grand View Research, “Global Containerized Data Center Market Size & Outlook” https://www.grandviewresearch.com/horizon/outlook/containerized-data-center-market-size/global Second Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights Revenue: Sales, net of returns and allowances, for the second quarter of 2026 were $3.6 million, compared to $0.8 million in the second quarter of 2025 on a GAAP basis. On a pro forma combined basis, revenue for the second quarter of 2025 was $6.4 million. For the first half of 2026, revenue was $7.9 million, roughly in line with pro forma combined revenue of $8.2 million in the first half of 2025. Vehicles Delivered: The Company delivered 26 vehicles during the second quarter of 2026, compared to 4 vehicles in the second quarter of 2025. Cost of Sales: Cost of sales for the second quarter of 2026 was $11.0 million, resulting in a gross loss of $7.5 million, consistent with the first quarter. The Company continues to expect gross margin to improve as production volumes at Union City scale and the cost benefits of the combined platform are realized. Operating Expenses: Total operating expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $11.9 million. Selling, general and administrative expenses were $7.8 million, reflecting the costs of running the combined company, partly offset by merger-related synergies, including reductions in redundant headcount and other operating costs. Research and development expenses were $4.1 million, reflecting continued strategic investment in the Company's bill of materials cost reduction program and early-stage engineering work supporting the mobile AI data center product line. Operating Loss: Operating loss was $19.4 million in the second quarter of 2026, compared to $9.0 million in the second quarter of 2025. Net Loss: Net loss for the second quarter of 2026 was $20.2 million, or $1.86 per basic and diluted share, compared to a net loss of $12.8 million, or $1.38 per share, in the same period last year. Capital Position: As of June 30, 2026, the Company had $9.6 million in cash and cash equivalents, plus $0.7 million of restricted cash. During the first half of 2026, the Company drew $20.0 million under its Cash Flow Credit Agreement, bringing the outstanding balance to $30.0 million, and drew $18.3 million under its Customer Order Credit Agreement. Subsequent to quarter end, the Company amended its Cash Flow Credit Agreement to increase capacity and borrowed an additional $10 million to fund its operations. cash and no outstanding debt Under purchase agreement for approximately $59 million incremental senior housing acquisition Janus Living, Inc. is a pure-play senior housing real estate investment trust that owns high-quality communities across the United States, and is majority owned by Healthpeak. Healthpeak owns 214.7 million shares of Janus Living common stock and operating partnership common units, representing a 73.6% equity ownership as of June 30, 2026. Janus Living is consolidated into Healthpeak’s financial statements, with the approximately 26.4% not owned by Healthpeak reported as noncontrolling interest. NORTHSIDE OUTPATIENT MEDICAL DEVELOPMENT In June 2026, Healthpeak entered into a development agreement for a new $20 million, 33,000 square foot outpatient medical building in the Sugar Hill submarket of Atlanta, Georgia. The development is 84% pre-leased to Northside Hospital and affiliated physician groups supporting a range of clinical services and extends Northside’s network in a high-growth submarket connecting its Forsyth and Gwinnett hospital campuses. The development represents Healthpeak’s fifth ground-up project totaling 565,000 square feet supporting Northside Hospital’s continued outpatient expansion in the Atlanta market. OUTPATIENT MEDICAL JOINT VENTURE RECAPITALIZATION As previously disclosed, in July 2026, Healthpeak entered into a joint venture with affiliates of Brookfield Asset Management (“Brookfield”) through the contribution of an 86-property outpatient medical portfolio valued at approximately $2.1 billion. The portfolio comprises approximately 5.6 million square feet and is located across 11 states including Kentucky, Indiana, Pennsylvania, Arkansas, Illinois, Minnesota, New Jersey, and New York. The portfolio is 95% leased with a weighted average remaining lease term of six years. Under the terms of the joint venture, Brookfield owns a 49% non-controlling equity interest and Healthpeak retains a 51% interest in the joint venture and serves as managing member, providing asset and property management services and earning customary fees. Healthpeak received proceeds of approximately $1.025 billion for the sale of the 49% interest. The transaction implies a trailing cash capitalization rate of approximately 5.9% and a valuation of approximately $380 per square foot. Healthpeak retains a call right for a finite period beginning after year seven to repurchase Brookfield’s interest at a price sufficient to provide Brookfield with a 6.5% net annual rate of return excluding initial transaction expenses. The joint venture advances Healthpeak’s capital allocation strategy by generating proceeds to strengthen its balance sheet, fund investment opportunities, and support long-term growth. The transaction establishes a structure by which the parties can expand their relationship over time and also underscores the differentiated platform Healthpeak has built, including deep health system relationships and ongoing investments across the enterprise in technology, systems, and innovation that enhance long-term portfolio performance. SELLER FINANCING LOAN REPAYMENT AND OTHER DISPOSITIONS In June 2026, Healthpeak received approximately $400 million of gross proceeds from the partial repayment of a seller financing loan. The remaining $20 million loan balance was extended by 12 months pursuant to contractual extension rights. The repayment resulted in a one-time $9 million increase in interest income from the accelerated recognition of the remaining fair value discount. During the second quarter of 2026, Healthpeak closed on $40 million of non-core outpatient medical dispositions at a trailing cash capitalization rate of 4.9%. BALANCE SHEET In June 2026, Healthpeak repaid $142 million of mortgage debt. Subsequent to the end of the second quarter, Healthpeak used proceeds from the Brookfield joint venture to repay $650 million of 3.25% senior notes at maturity and approximately $375 million of borrowings under its commercial paper program. As of August 3, 2026, Healthpeak had $3.4 billion of liquidity including cash and available credit facility capacity. SHARE REPURCHASE ACTIVITY AND NEW SHARE REPURCHASE AUTHORIZATION As previously disclosed, in April 2026, Healthpeak repurchased 5.9 million common shares at a weighted average share price of $16.81 for approximately $100 million under its $500 million share repurchase program. In July 2026, Healthpeak's Board of Directors authorized a new $500 million share repurchase program, replacing the existing $500 million authorization. The shares may be repurchased through various methods, including in the open market at Healthpeak's discretion and subject to market conditions, regulatory requirements, and other customary conditions. DIVIDEND On July 9, 2026, Healthpeak's Board of Directors declared a monthly common stock cash dividend of $0.10167 per share for each of July, August, and September of 2026, representing cash dividends totaling $0.305 per share for the third quarter, and an annualized dividend amount of $1.22 per share.
